title: The Alphabet & Sounds
subtitle: Learn the 26 letters of English and how to spell your name out loud.
objectives: Say the 26 letters of the English alphabet
Spell your own name out loud, letter by letter
Understand simple classroom questions like "How do you spell that?"

content.intro: English has 26 letters. Some sound similar to Portuguese, and some are very different. Listen to each letter, then practice saying it.

rules.heading: The 26 letters
rules.body:
LettersSounds a bit like (Portuguese)
A, H, J, Kei / eitch / djei / kei
B, C, D, E, G, P, T, V, Zbi / si / di / i / dji / pi / ti / vi / zi
F, L, M, N, S, Xéf / él / ém / én / és / éks
I, Yai / uai
Oôu
Q, U, Wquiú / iú / dâbliu
Rar (English R, not rolled)

This is only a rough guide — the best way to learn the real sounds is to listen to a native speaker or a recording, not just read the guide.

rules.heading: Spelling out loud
rules.body:
To spell a word, say each letter separately.

  • How do you spell your name? — M-A-R-I-A. (M, A, R, I, A)
  • How do you spell "cat"? — C-A-T.

For a double letter, say "double": B-A-double L (ball).

exercises.instructions: Match each letter to the sound it's closest to.

items.prompt: How many letters are there in the English alphabet?
"How do you spell your name?" is a question about...
items.explanation: "Spell" means to say the letters of a word one by one.

items.prompt: Which letter comes right after "C" in the alphabet?
items.explanation: A, B, C, D — "D" comes after "C."

exercises.title: Spell It Out
exercises.instructions: Type the letters of your own first name, separated by dashes. Example: M-A-R-I-A.

items.prompt: Spell your first name, one letter at a time (use dashes between letters).

summary: English has 26 letters — practice saying each one out loud.
"How do you spell that?" asks someone to say a word letter by letter.
For a repeated letter, say "double" (double L, double O).
